themes_detail.label: Dead animals & unsanitary conditions spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints and unsanitary animal conditions on private property surged to 4 complaints last week—a 1500% spike from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66)—suggesting a potential pest infestation, wildlife die-off event, or sanitation crisis in the district this week.
evidence: 4 dead animal complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
4 unsanitary animal private property complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Concurrent spike in missed collection complaints (3 last week vs. 0.2 avg) suggests potential sanitation system breakdown
reporting_angles: Interview residents and 311 complainants about specific locations and circumstances of animal discoveries—rodent colony, disease vector, or isolated incidents?
Contact DSNY and Parks Dept. to understand whether this reflects a real surge or a reporting artifact; obtain historical data on seasonal patterns

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 96 last week—a 278% spike from the 25.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.98)—indicating a surge in construction, new venue openings, or late-night commercial activity in Morningside Heights this week.
evidence: 96 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 25.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (278% increase, z-score: 5.98)
364 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (321 alterations) suggest active construction environment
1727 Amsterdam Avenue Hill Top Apartments development in public review may be driving construction-related noise
reporting_angles: Map the 96 complaints to identify geographic cluster—is noise concentrated around construction sites, new bars/restaurants, or Columbia University expansion?
Interview residents near active construction or late-night venues about impact on sleep and quality of life; cross-reference with 311 addresses

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures surge
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 28 last week—a 234% spike from the 8.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.34)—affecting residents in aging residential buildings in the district this week, potentially linked to winter demand or deferred maintenance.
evidence: 28 elevator complaints last week vs. 8.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (234% increase, z-score: 5.34)
Concurrent spike in building code violations (SPIT complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.6 avg, z-score: 4.85) suggests systemic maintenance failures
District's long-standing request for 'repair or upgrade subway stations or other transit infrastructure' reflects broader infrastructure decay pattern
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 elevator complaint addresses and contact building owners to investigate whether complaints reflect aging buildings, inadequate maintenance contracts, or parts shortages
Interview elderly residents and people with mobility challenges about impact of elevator outages on access to apartments and services

themes_detail.label: Outside building debris spike
themes_detail.summary: Outside building complaints jumped to 6 last week—a 700% spike from the 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.94)—suggesting active outdoor construction, illegal dumping, or sanitation breakdowns outside residential buildings this week.
evidence: 6 'outside building' complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 7.94)
Concurrent spikes in missed collection (3 complaints, 1100% increase) suggest DSNY capacity or routing issues
321 active alteration permits suggest ongoing construction debris generation district-wide
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 6 outside building complaints with active DOB permits to determine if debris is tied to legitimate construction or illegal dumping
Contact DSNY about missed pickups and communicate with block associations to understand whether illegal dumping is occurring

themes_detail.label: Building/Use code violations
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use violations spiked 3 weeks ago to 7 complaints—a 300% spike from the 1.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.82)—suggesting non-compliant conversions, overcrowding, or illegal short-term rentals in the district.
evidence: 7 building/use violations 3 weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% increase, z-score: 4.82)
1727 Amsterdam Avenue ULURP application in public review may be triggering heightened code scrutiny in district
District's recurring budget request to 'study land use and zoning' reflects ongoing misalignment between permitted and actual use
reporting_angles: Obtain list of 7 violations from 3 weeks ago and investigate whether they reflect short-term rental conversions, illegal subdivisions, or other residential misuse
Interview community board members and CB101 budget requesters about zoning enforcement capacity and whether violations are concentrated near Columbia University properties
